question: Are L1's finite, deterministic but batching-sensitive deviations floating-point amplification or an incorrect kernel?
hypothesis: Higher inference precision will reduce discrepancies while retaining learned parameters and the declared tolerances.

sources.sections: Floating-point precision; batched versus sliced computations; CPU/GPU differences
sources.consequence: Test precision and attention backend separately; do not infer corruption from small absolute deviations alone.
Keep calibrated inference moments fixed during this precision experiment.

differences: This is an inference/runtime precision intervention on local ROCm kernels, not a new scientific architecture or training run. CPU is used solely as a numerical reference.
contrary_evidence: Float64 agreement alone cannot show that all original float32 training updates were accurate; it only establishes a stable inference implementation for these learned weights.

protocol.inputs: All six A001 step-40000 calibrated snapshots
protocol.selection: Prefer float32_math only if all six pass; otherwise use float64_math for all six if all pass; otherwise block. Do not change tolerances.

success: Every encoder/predictor output and gradient passes CPU/GPU and grouping checks under a common policy, with finite state.
stop: No passing common policy blocks learned interpretation; no change to original training jobs without reproduced corruption.
